interactionTexts: Ibuprofen can reduce the effect of some blood pressure medicines.
Use the product leaflet or pharmacist advice to decide whether monitoring is needed.
Vitamin C may affect certain laboratory test results at higher doses.
Ibuprofen and acetylsalicylic acid are both NSAID-related pain medicines and may increase gastrointestinal irritation.
Combining NSAIDs can increase the risk of serious side effects such as stomach ulcers.
Drinking too much alcohol while taking aspirin can irritate the stomach.
The combination may be relevant for customers with stomach problems or bleeding risk.
Drinking a lot of alcohol while taking ibuprofen can increase the risk of side effects.
The warning is especially relevant when ibuprofen is taken at higher doses or for longer periods.
Regular heavy alcohol use can make paracetamol safety checks more important.
Customers should follow the product leaflet and ask a healthcare professional when unsure.
Grapefruit juice can affect the way some medicines are processed by the body.
For simvastatin-like products, grapefruit may increase the risk of unwanted effects.
Warfarin and acetylsalicylic acid can both affect bleeding risk.
This combination should be checked carefully before a customer-facing warning is suppressed.
Warfarin and ibuprofen may increase bleeding risk when used together.
A frontend widget should show this as a pair interaction only when both ingredients are present.
